title: Texas Smoked Pulled Pork Shoulder
seoTitle: Texas Smoked Pulled Pork Shoulder | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Texas pit-style shoulder that pulls clean and holds all shift
subtitle: Salt-and-pepper shoulder, no sweet sauce, and pickles for ten
description: Adapted from classic Texas smoked pork shoulder tradition (Hey Grill Hey, BBQ Pit Boys): bone-in shoulder gets a simple salt-and-pepper rub, smokes over oak until 203°F, and pulls with defatted drippings—no sweet sauce.

steps.title: Season Texas-style
steps.instruction: Coat shoulder with mustard. Pack salt, pepper, and garlic powder on all sides. Rest 20 minutes while smoker heats to 275°F with oak.

steps.title: Smoke the shoulder
steps.instruction: Smoke fat-side up at 275°F until bark is dark and internal temp reaches 165°F, about 4–5 hours.

steps.title: Wrap and finish
steps.instruction: Wrap in foil with a splash of apple cider vinegar. Continue at 275°F until probe-tender and 203°F, about 2–3 hours.

steps.title: Rest and pull
steps.instruction: Rest wrapped 40 minutes. Skim fat from juices. Pull pork, mixing in defatted drippings to moisten.

steps.title: 170°F warm hold
steps.instruction: Transfer to hotel pan, cover with foil, hold at 170°F. Stir before service if top dries.
Pulled pork tray with pickles, onion, white bread, and hot sauce on the side. Texas-style—no sweet glaze.

steps.title: Leftovers
steps.instruction: Reheat covered at 325°F with splash of broth until 165°F. Use in breakfast tacos with eggs.

proTips: 275°F speeds the cook vs 225°F—still tender if you hit 203°F.
Skim fat from drippings or pulled pork turns greasy on the hold line.
Hot sauce on the side keeps purists and heat-seekers both happy.
tonightSpread: Pulled pork in a hotel pan.
Pickles, onion, white bread, and hot sauce.
leftovers: Texas pork breakfast tacos with scrambled eggs.
Mix into smoked baked beans for second-day depth.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Texas pork is about smoke and meat, not sugar. It holds at 170°F for hours and pairs with pickles and white bread like brisket.
mealPrepNotes: Start early. Wrap when bark color is right. Hold pulled pork covered at 170°F with a splash of defatted drippings. Pickles and onions stay cold on ice.
